title: Probability: Venn Diagrams, Mutually Exclusive and Complementary Events
seo_title: Grade 10 Probability Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Compare the relative frequency of an experimental outcome with the theoretical probability of the outcome; Venn diagrams as an aid to solving probability problems; mutually exclusive events and complementary events; the identity for any two events A and B: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B).
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 10 probability worksheets: sample spaces, Venn diagrams, the addition rule, mutually exclusive and complementary events. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B).
body_html:
How to think about it

  • P(event) = number of favourable outcomesnumber of possible outcomes.
  • Addition rule: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B).
  • Mutually exclusive events cannot happen together: P(A and B) = 0.
  • Complementary events: P(not A) = 1 − P(A).

Examples

Example

P(A) = 0,5; P(B) = 0,4; P(A and B) = 0,2

0,5 + 0,4 − 0,2

Answer: P(A or B) = 0,7

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The overlapSubtract P(A and B).
Mutually exclusiveThey have no overlap.
The complementP(not A) = 1 − P(A).

items.q: A coin is flipped and a fair spinner with 5 equal sections (red, blue, green, yellow, white) is spun. How many outcomes are possible?
items.e: 2 outcomes for the coin × 5 for the spinner = 10.

items.q: Two fair dice are rolled and the scores are multiplied. What is the probability of a product less than 12?
items.e: Draw a 6 × 6 sample space: 36 equally likely outcomes. 19 of them give a product less than 12, so P = 1936.

items.q: Two fair dice are rolled and the scores are added. What is the probability of a sum of 9?
items.e: Draw a 6 × 6 sample space: 36 equally likely outcomes. 4 of them give a sum of 9, so P = 436 = 19.

items.q: P(A) = 0,7, P(B) = 0,3 and P(A and B) = 0,1. Find P(A or B).
items.e: Addition Rule: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B) = 0,7 + 0,3 − 0,1 = 0,9. Subtract the overlap so it is not counted twice.

items.q: P(A) = 0,5, P(B) = 0,7 and P(A and B) = 0,4. Find P(A or B).
items.e: Addition Rule: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B) = 0,5 + 0,7 − 0,4 = 0,8. Subtract the overlap so it is not counted twice.

items.q: One card is drawn from a standard 52-card deck. What is the probability it is a heart or a king?
items.e: 13 hearts + 4 kings − 1 king of hearts (counted twice) = 16 cards. 16/52 = 413.

items.q: The probability that it rains tomorrow is 0,35. What is the probability that it does not rain?
items.e: Complement: P(not A) = 1 − P(A) = 1 − 0,35 = 0,65.

items.q: Events A and B are mutually exclusive (they cannot both happen). P(A) = 0,2 and P(B) = 0,2. Find P(A or B).
items.e: Mutually exclusive events have no overlap, so P(A and B) = 0 and P(A or B) = 0,2 + 0,2 = 0,4.
